s01_clean_backport: One fix promoted dev -> uat -> prod with cherry-pick -x, no conflicts. Baseline.
s02_prod_hotfix_vs_dev_fix: Core case. prod got a hotfix on the same line a dev fix changes. Backporting the dev fix to prod conflicts.
s03_modified_backport_with_trailer: Backport had to be edited during conflict resolution, so patch-id no longer matches. The -x trailer is the only exact link.
s04_backport_no_trailer_reworded: Same change re-typed by hand on prod: different author, message, variable name. No trailer, patch-id differs. Only fuzzy matching can link them.
s05_whitespace_only_difference: Backport differs only in whitespace and has no trailer. git patch-id ignores whitespace, so the match is exact.
s06_clone_without_metadata: Same history as s02, but use clone/ — a plain git clone of repo/. Clones do not fetch refs/notes/*, and the sidecar test_records.json belongs to repo/ only.
s07_both_sides_untested: Same conflict as s02, but neither side was ever tested or deployed. Records exist for other commits, so the answer is 'unverified', not 'unknown'.
s08_rename_then_conflict: File renamed on dev; prod hotfix made in the old path. Forward-porting the hotfix conflicts in the NEW path.
s09_modify_delete: dev deleted a file that prod hot-fixed. Merging prod back into dev gives a modify/delete conflict (no conflict markers in any file).
s10_multi_hunk_mixed_provenance: Two conflict hunks in one file. On the prod side, hunk 1 comes from a deployed hotfix but hunk 2 comes from a commit that sits on prod and was NEVER deployed.
s11_failed_test_reverted_then_reapplied: uat tried a fix (failed test), reverted it, then landed v2 (passed). Backporting v2 to prod conflicts with a prod hotfix.
s12_squashed_backport: Three dev commits squashed into one prod commit (Django-style 'Backport of' lines).
s13_test_was_on_older_commit: uat has a passing test, but on an OLDER commit. The line in conflict was last changed by a later, untested commit.
s14_criss_cross_merge: Branches merged into each other (criss-cross), so there are TWO merge bases.
s15_recurring_conflict_rerere: The same conflict was already resolved (and tested) on uat. Merging dev into release hits it again; rerere replays the old resolution.
s16_chained_backport: dev -> uat -> prod, where prod picked the UAT copy (not the dev original). The prod commit carries TWO cherry-pick trailers.
s17_chain_modified_midway: Chain where the FIRST hop was hand-edited and the second hop was clean. prod copy is identical to the UAT version, not to the dev original.
s18_resolution_introduces_new_code: The s02 conflict was resolved by WRITING NEW CODE (0.025 from ours + tiers from theirs). Both inputs had test evidence; the result has none.
s19_resolution_mixes_hunks: Two-hunk conflict (s10) resolved by taking OURS for hunk 1 and THEIRS for hunk 2.
s20_same_patch_different_base: Clean cherry-pick with IDENTICAL patch-id, but the fix calls normalize(), which is defined in an earlier dev commit that was never backported. prod is now broken.
s21_rebased_after_test: A commit was tested, then the branch was rebased: the tested SHA is no longer on any branch, and the new SHA has no record of its own.
s22_notes_diverged_between_clones: Two people added provenance to the same commit in different clones. QA pushed first; Ops' plain notes fetch is now rejected (non-fast-forward).
s23_trailer_points_to_missing_commit: prod commit says '(cherry picked from commit X)' but X was force-pushed away and garbage-collected. A test note for X still exists.
s24_lying_trailer: Commit message claims to be a cherry-pick of a tested fix, but the code is unrelated (it removes the refund fee). Messages are claims, not evidence.
s25_deploy_rollback: p2 was deployed, then production was rolled back to p1 (see 'at' order in records). The prod branch still points at p2.
s26_flaky_test_history: The dev side was tested three times in uat: pass, FAIL, pass.
s27_test_on_descendant: CI tested only the uat tip. The conflicted line comes from an earlier commit, but it is unchanged in the tested tip. (Opposite of s13.)
s28_evil_merge: The conflicting dev line was introduced INSIDE a merge commit (an 'evil merge'), not by any regular commit.
s29_github_squash_merge: GitHub-style squash merge: PR #42 (2 commits, CI passed on its head) became ONE commit on dev with a new SHA and only '(#42)' in the subject. The branch is deleted; refs/pull/42/head remains, like on GitHub.
s30_partial_backport: Only one of the two files changed by the original was backported.
s31_conflict_mid_sequence: Backporting a RANGE of 3 commits: the first applies, the second conflicts, the third is still pending in .git/sequencer/todo.
s32_rebase_inverts_ours_theirs: Rebasing 'feature' onto dev conflicts. During a rebase, HEAD/'ours' is the UPSTREAM (dev), and 'theirs' is YOUR commit being replayed — the reverse of a merge.
s33_revert_conflict: Reverting an old commit whose line was changed again later.
s34_diff3_and_custom_marker_size: Repo uses merge.conflictStyle=diff3 (extra '||||||| base' section) and .md files use 12-character conflict markers.
s35_literal_markers_in_content: A committed test fixture legitimately contains conflict markers. Only app/payment.py is actually in conflict.
s36_rename_rename_and_add_add: Both sides renamed the same file to DIFFERENT names, and both added app/config.py with different contents.
s37_unicode_paths_crlf_and_modes: Conflict in a path with spaces and non-ASCII characters, in a CRLF file. The script merges cleanly but must end up executable (mode from prod, content from dev).
s38_shallow_clone: Use shallow/ — a --depth 2 clone. The prod line's real origin (the hotfix) is beyond the shallow boundary, so blame wrongly points at the boundary commit.
s39_same_fix_two_paths: The same fix reached prod twice: once by cherry-pick (deployed), and again via a uat -> prod promotion. git merges it cleanly.
s40_large_history: 225 commits, one 800-line file, 25 conflict hunks. Every hunk has a different origin commit on each side. CI ran only on dev tip; deploy only on prod tip.
s41_both_sides_variants_of_same_fix: The SAME dev fix was hand-backported twice, differently, to uat and prod. Merging uat into prod makes the two variants of one fix conflict with each other.
s42_code_moved_between_files: dev MOVED refund() into another file; prod hot-fixed it in the old place. git sees 'deleted vs modified lines' — the hotfix would be silently lost if 'ours' is taken.
s43_formatter_commit_hides_origin: The dev line was last touched by a whitespace-only formatter commit listed in .git-blame-ignore-revs. The real origin is the commit before it.
s44_tested_trailer_without_ci: The dev commit's message CLAIMS 'Tested-in: production', but CI/deploy records have nothing for it. A self-written trailer is not evidence.
s45_rollback_records_out_of_order: Same rollback story as s25, but the records were appended out of order. Only the 'at' timestamps tell the truth: p1 (Oct 1) -> p2 (Oct 2) -> p1 again (Oct 3).
s46_symlink_conflict: A symlink was re-pointed differently on each side. No text, no markers — the conflict is between two link targets (mode 120000).
s47_submodule_conflict: Submodule pointer conflict: dev moved lib to v2, prod moved it to a v1.1 security fix. The 'file' in conflict is a gitlink, not text.
s48_mixed_origins_in_one_hunk: ONE hunk whose prod side mixes two commits: line 1 deployed, line 2 never deployed. The hunk is only as trustworthy as its weakest line.
s49_reverted_fix_reintroduced_by_merge: NO conflict — that's the trap. The fix failed in production and was reverted there, but dev still has the original. 'git merge dev' silently brings the bad fix back.
s50_deep_history: The dev line's origin is 5000 commits deep; CI only ran on the dev tip. Any per-commit subprocess loop will time out.
s51_non_utf8_and_no_final_newline: One conflicted file is Latin-1 (not UTF-8); the other has no newline at end of file.
s52_deletion_vs_modification: prod's side of the hunk is EMPTY: the hotfix deleted those lines. Blame has nothing to point at; the origin is the commit that deleted them.
s53_original_only_in_remote_ref: The original commit is reachable ONLY from refs/remotes/upstream/main (like a fork tracking upstream). No local branch contains it.
s54_git_am_backport: Backport by e-mailed patch (git format-patch | git am -3), Linux-kernel style. There is no CHERRY_PICK_HEAD and no trailer — the original is only identifiable by its diff.
s55_conflict_in_linked_worktree: The conflict happens in a linked worktree, where .git is a FILE pointing elsewhere and CHERRY_PICK_HEAD lives in .git/worktrees/<name>/.
s56_squash_merge_conflict: 'git merge --squash' conflict: there is NO MERGE_HEAD. The incoming commits are only listed in .git/SQUASH_MSG.
s57_partially_resolved: Two files conflict; the developer already resolved app/legacy.py (git add). The tool is run halfway through the resolution.
s58_ambiguous_short_sha: The backport message says 'Backport of f691a', but TWO commits start with that prefix (git rev-parse refuses: ambiguous). Only the code tells which one is meant.
s59_noisy_provenance_records: The dev commit's note mixes good and bad data: a uat pass, a FAILED production deploy, an unknown env, an unknown record kind, and a line that isn't JSON.
s60_cherry_picked_merge_commit: A whole merged PR was backported with 'git cherry-pick -m 1 <merge>'. The trailer names a MERGE commit, whose plain 'git show' diff is empty.
s61_empty_cherry_pick: Cherry-pick stops with NO conflict: the change is already on prod (applied by hand), so the pick is empty. git just says 'now empty'.
r01_changelog_both_added: Merging PR #12: both PRs added a line at the same spot in CHANGELOG.md. Safe to fix automatically: keep both entries.
r02_requirements_both_added: Both sides appended dependencies at the end of requirements.txt, and BOTH added rich==13.7.0. Keep every dependency exactly once (naive 'keep both' duplicates rich).
r03_whitespace_only_side: main's side of the conflict is a whitespace-only formatter change; the PR's side is real logic. Safe to fix automatically: keep the PR's logic.
r04_pr_carries_stale_copy_of_fix: The PR branch carries an OLD copy of a fix (cherry-picked) that main has since improved and deployed. Keep main's line (the PR's version is already in main's history, by patch-id) plus the PR's own refund change.
r05_previous_tested_resolution: The identical conflict was already resolved on main (rate = 0.019) and that resolution passed uat. Reuse it (rerere is enabled and has it recorded).
r06_both_sides_logic_unverified: Both sides changed the fee logic differently and neither was tested. Picking one is a business decision: the tool must NOT auto-resolve; it must stop and explain.
r07_mixed_safe_and_unsafe_files: CHANGELOG.md is safe to fix, app/payment.py is not. The tool must not commit a half-resolved merge: app/payment.py must still be in conflict afterwards.
r08_code_moved_needs_reapply: main moved refund() to app/refunds.py; the PR hot-fixed it in the old place. Taking either side loses something (tests fail). Correct fix: keep the move AND re-apply the hotfix in app/refunds.py — or refuse and explain.
r09_backport_compatible_intents: Backporting a fix to release conflicts with a production hotfix on the next line. The two intents are compatible; only a COMBINATION passes both sides' tests. The result must keep the -x trailer and be a 1-parent commit.
r10_rebase_pr_onto_main: 'Rebase and merge' style PR: rebasing pr-7 onto main conflicts with a formatter commit. The tool must resolve AND finish the rebase (HEAD back on pr-7, on top of main). Remember: during a rebase 'ours' is main.
